slides.title: Question 1: Threading vs Multiprocessing
slides.prompt: Why is `multiprocessing` preferred over `threading` in Python for CPU-bound tasks?
options: Multiprocessing creates separate Python processes, each with its own GIL and memory space to achieve parallel CPU execution
Threading uses more RAM than process creation
Threading cannot run on multi-core processors
Multiprocessing code runs asynchronously without locks
slides.correctAnswer: Multiprocessing creates separate Python processes, each with its own GIL and memory space to achieve parallel CPU execution

slides.title: Question 5: Daemon Threads
slides.prompt: What happens to Daemon Threads when the main program finishes execution and exits?
options: Daemon threads are abruptly terminated immediately
The main program waits for daemon threads to finish
Daemon threads are converted to background processes
slides.correctAnswer: Daemon threads are abruptly terminated immediately

slides.title: Question 8: Semaphore Usage
slides.prompt: How does a `Semaphore` differ from a standard `Lock`?
options: A Semaphore permits a fixed maximum number of concurrent accesses via an internal counter
A Semaphore can only be used with multiprocessing
A Semaphore does not require release calls
slides.correctAnswer: A Semaphore permits a fixed maximum number of concurrent accesses via an internal counter

slides.title: Question 9: Inter-Process Communication
slides.prompt: Fill in the thread/process safe queue class used for message passing between concurrent tasks.

slides.title: Question 10: RLock (Reentrant Lock)
slides.prompt: When should an `RLock` (Reentrant Lock) be used instead of a standard `Lock`?
options: When the same thread needs to acquire the lock multiple times recursively without blocking itself
When speed is more critical than synchronization
When sharing resources with C extensions
slides.correctAnswer: When the same thread needs to acquire the lock multiple times recursively without blocking itself

slides.correctAnswer: I/O-bound tasks (network requests, file operations, database queries)
